public_rationale: Accessible reporting describes Amazon storing hardware ahead of powered deployment. That makes the underlying practice plausible, but it does not establish a USD 200 billion aggregate across the named firms and others. The reporting also concerns a later period. There is no comparable comprehensive estimate low enough to contradict the claim.
limitations: The strongest accessible inventory reporting is secondary and concerns one company.
The company population and valuation basis are partly inferred.
No current-period aggregate inventory measurement was retrieved.

conditions: chips they either can't plug in or simply want to have in supply

statement.excerpt: Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Meta, Oracle, and far too many other companies have been hoarding hundreds of billions of dollars of AI chips that they either (to quote Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella) can’t plug in or simply want to have in supply for reasons that I find tough to imagine.

from_speaker: hundreds of billions of dollars of AI chips
can’t plug in or simply want to have in supply
our_interpretation: Read 'hundreds of billions' as at least USD 200 billion collectively, not that amount at each company.
Read 'hoarding' as holding purchased chips unused pending deployment or as reserves; no separate claim about wrongful intent is required.
Value chips at acquisition cost, excluding buildings, power equipment and unfulfilled purchase commitments.
Use April–June 2026, the latest completed calendar quarter broadly reportable by the named customers before the post.
The estimated accounting basis follows the surrounding discussion of inferred unused-chip values, rather than a cited company inventory total.
criteria.support_condition: Reliable company-level inventory evidence establishes aggregate unused or reserve AI chip acquisition value of at least USD 200 billion across the named firms and an identified set of other purchasers.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A sufficiently comprehensive, comparable inventory estimate places the total below USD 200 billion, with uncertainty that excludes that threshold.
